fluff.overview:
The Gauss-Buster is a one-of-a-kind MilitiaMech conversion performed by the Mississauga Militia in 3134, born from desperation and ingenuity on a Lyran backwater world several jumps from the Jade Falcon border. When the HPG network collapsed and military action escalated across the Sphere, the small garrison on Mississauga (too insignificant to warrant regular LCAF defenders) was forced to improvise its own defenses from whatever equipment was available.

The project began when the militia's most potent asset, a BXK-F7 Hollander II, was sidelined with fusion reactor damage. With no replacement parts available, the militia's technicians salvaged the heavy Gauss rifle and sought a chassis large enough to mount it. The Buster HaulerMech, with its spacious frame and sure-footed stance, proved the only viable candidate. The resulting Gauss-Buster is best understood as a lightly mobile turret rather than a true combat machine, dependent on an external power source connected by armored cable to fire its primary weapon.
fluff.capabilities:
The Gauss-Buster retains the Buster's standard fifty-ton industrial chassis and 150-rated ICE engine, providing the same plodding maximum speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour. The heavy Gauss rifle mounted in the right torso represents devastating firepower for a machine of this class, capable of threatening even assault-weight BattleMechs at extreme range. However, the ICE powerplant cannot generate sufficient energy to charge the weapon's capacitors, requiring the Gauss-Buster to remain physically connected to an external power source via an armored charging cable at all times during combat operations.

This tethered arrangement severely limits the machine's tactical flexibility. An infantry platoon is required to manage the cable connection, typically housing a portable power source in an armored personnel carrier positioned nearby. Connecting or disconnecting the cable takes approximately one minute, and the unit must remain stationary while plugged in to avoid severing the connection and potentially damaging both the cable and the weapon. The militia's technicians upgraded the armor to heavy industrial grade and installed an advanced fire control system, though ammunition capacity is limited to just four rounds, a constraint deemed acceptable given the extreme unlikelihood of the Gauss-Buster surviving long enough to exhaust its supply.
fluff.history:
The Gauss-Buster emerged from a specific crisis on Mississauga in 3134, shortly after the HPG Blackout threw the Inner Sphere into chaos. The planet's isolation and proximity to the Jade Falcon border made self-defense an urgent priority, but the tiny local militia lacked the resources to procure proper military hardware. When their sole BattleMech (a Hollander II) suffered irreparable reactor damage, the militia's technical staff, led by Chief Technician Francis Zappa, devised the unconventional solution of transplanting the salvaged heavy Gauss rifle onto a common Buster HaulerMech.

The conversion required considerable improvisation to overcome the fundamental incompatibility between an energy-intensive weapon system and an ICE-powered chassis. The armored charging cable and external power source arrangement that resulted was crude but functional, transforming the Gauss-Buster into what the militia themselves described as a mobile turret. The machine's heavy industrial armor and advanced fire control system (both scavenged from the damaged Hollander II) gave it a degree of battlefield survivability that belied its industrial origins.

Reports from Mississauga suggest the militia has continued developing similar cable-powered weapon installations on industrial chassis, creating improvised power hookups near likely defensive positions that allow the Gauss-Buster to connect and engage targets rapidly. Whether this concept has spread to other militia forces remains unclear, but the basic principle of mounting salvaged heavy weapons on available IndustrialMech platforms became increasingly common across the Inner Sphere during the Dark Age.
fluff.deployment: The sole known Gauss-Buster conversion is a customized Buster HaulerMech operated by the Mississauga Militia, produced by mounting a salvaged heavy Gauss rifle from a disabled Hollander II onto the fifty-ton industrial chassis. The conversion includes heavy industrial armor, an advanced fire control system, and the distinctive armored charging cable that connects the machine to an external power source. Limited to four rounds of ammunition and effectively stationary during combat, the Gauss-Buster functions as a mobile turret that can be repositioned between engagements but must remain tethered while firing. The militia has reportedly pre-positioned power hookups at defensive sites across Mississauga, allowing the Gauss-Buster to connect and engage approaching threats with minimal setup time.
